response: Yes, acute fibrinous and organizing pneumonia (AFOP) can be an expression of immune dysregulation. In a pediatric case, AFOP was found to be part of an autoimmune syndrome, which also included hepatic failure and very severe aplastic anemia (VSAA). The patient's favorable outcome after immunosuppressive therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation suggests that AFOP may be the result of immune dysregulation. This implies that immune dysregulation can play a role in the development of AFOP, and treatment targeting the immune system may be effective in managing the condition.
